title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Premium Revision Paper #2

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the seed activity, why do we plant two tins? (1 mark)
   A. To compare seeds with water and seeds without water
   B. To use up all the soil
   C. Because one tin is too small
   D. To make it look neat

2. Which is a good way to collect free water for the home? (1 mark)
   A. Buying bottled water only
   B. Collecting rainwater from a roof
   C. Taking water from a neighbour
   D. Digging a hole in the road

3. Which of these is a Kenyan water body mentioned in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. River Beas
   B. River Rijubalika
   C. Lake Victoria
   D. River Ganga

4. In a maize farm, what does the wind that carries pollen represent among the elements? (1 mark)
   A. Agni
   B. Jal
   C. Vayu
   D. Prithvi

5. Why is it a mistake to say there are four elements in the Panch Mahabhoot? (1 mark)
   A. There is only one
   B. There are seven
   C. There are ten
   D. There are five

6. Which faith do Tulsi and the Ganga belong to most closely? (1 mark)
   A. Jainism
   B. Buddhism
   C. Hinduism
   D. Sikhism

7. Where was Hiranyakashipu when Narsimha stopped him? (1 mark)
   A. In a field
   B. On a mountain
   C. At the doorway, neither inside nor outside
   D. On a boat

8. Which Tirthankar is the twenty-third of Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. Buddha
   B. Mahavir
   C. Parshvanath
   D. Guru Nanak

9. In which city was Parshvanath born? (1 mark)
   A. Varanasi
   B. Nairobi
   C. Lumbini
   D. Lahore

10. Which of these is one of the six directions in the Sigalovada Sutta? (1 mark)
   A. Teachers
   B. Strangers
   C. Rivers
   D. Kings

11. What does the langar teach? (1 mark)
   A. Greed
   B. Equality
   C. Fear
   D. Pride

12. What does Bal Kaand tell about? (1 mark)
   A. The fourteen years in the forest
   B. The war with the demons
   C. The end of the story
   D. The childhood of Ram and his brothers

13. What is Ayodhya Kaand about? (1 mark)
   A. Yoga
   B. The birth of the Buddha
   C. Ram going to the forest and Bharat's humility
   D. The life of Guru Nanak

14. What is the Dhammapada? (1 mark)
   A. A book of maps
   B. A long story of a king
   C. A list of temples
   D. A book of wise sayings and verses

15. Which of these should you do first when learning a mantra? (1 mark)
   A. Say it very fast
   B. Guess the words
   C. Listen to a teacher or recording for correct sounds
   D. Skip the words

16. Which goddess is Saraswati? (1 mark)
   A. Goddess of fire
   B. Goddess of the river Ganga
   C. Goddess of knowledge and learning
   D. Goddess of war

17. How should we say the Gayatri Mantra? (1 mark)
   A. While eating
   B. Slowly and clearly, sitting quietly
   C. While running
   D. Shouting

18. What is a Mandir? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A Hindu place of worship
   C. A river
   D. A market

19. Who should be allowed to board first? (1 mark)
   A. The strongest
   B. Children, elders and people with disabilities
   C. The loudest
   D. The fastest

20. Which king is known for always telling the truth in a Hindu story? (1 mark)
   A. Hiranyakashipu
   B. Harishchandra
   C. Kansa
   D. Ravan

21. What does Sadachaar mean? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A holy river
   C. Daily prayer
   D. Good conduct

22. Which best describes a person with integrity? (1 mark)
   A. Loud
   B. Honest only when watched
   C. Honest even when nobody is watching
   D. Rich

23. What is the purpose of a lost and found corner? (1 mark)
   A. To hide them
   B. To sell lost items
   C. To keep the items forever
   D. To keep found items until owners claim them

24. Which is fair play in a game? (1 mark)
   A. Tripping others
   B. Following the rules even when nobody is looking
   C. Pushing
   D. Cheating

25. What should passengers do with rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it out of the window
   B. Drop it on the road
   C. Keep it until you find a bin
   D. Leave it on the seat

26. Which faith's story in the lesson is about honest earnings? (1 mark)
   A. Jainism
   B. Buddhism
   C. Hinduism
   D. Sikhism

27. What does the word yoga mean? (1 mark)
   A. To sleep
   B. To eat
   C. To join or unite
   D. To run

28. Who should guide children in yoga? (1 mark)
   A. A friend who has never tried
   B. Nobody
   C. A stranger
   D. A trained teacher or trusted adult

29. Which principle is about the Supreme Soul? (1 mark)
   A. Prani Daya
   B. Prarthana
   C. Paramatma
   D. Punarjanam

30. What does Dharma mean? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A river
   C. A sport
   D. The right way of living

31. According to the teaching, what happens to good actions? (1 mark)
   A. They bring bad luck
   B. They are forgotten
   C. They bring good results
   D. They have no results

32. What does Prani mean? (1 mark)
   A. A plant only
   B. A river
   C. A living being
   D. A stone

33. Which king protected a dove in a well-known story? (1 mark)
   A. Ravan
   B. Harishchandra
   C. King Shibi
   D. Hiranyakashipu

34. Because God sees all we do, what should we do? (1 mark)
   A. Be honest even when alone
   B. Complain
   C. Cheat
   D. Hide

35. Which of these is a way of following Artha? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting food
   B. Cheating
   C. Stealing
   D. Saving pocket money and not taking what is not yours

36. What do Jains say on the last day of Paryushan? (1 mark)
   A. Namaste
   B. Micchami Dukkadam
   C. Sat Sri Akal
   D. Om Namah Shivaya

37. Which festival comes last of the three studied? (1 mark)
   A. Maha Shivratri
   B. Paryushan Parva
   C. Yoga Day
   D. Madaraka Day

38. What does Utsav mean? (1 mark)
   A. Festival
   B. River
   C. Yoga
   D. Prayer

39. Which stories are told about Maha Shivratri? (1 mark)
   A. That it is a harvest festival of Kenya
   B. That it is a Jain festival of forgiveness
   C. That it is the night of Shiva and Parvati's wedding or of Shiva's great dance
   D. That it is the birth of the Buddha

40. What does vaar mean? (1 mark)
   A. Day of the week
   B. Month
   C. Year
   D. Planet

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Match each being with a teaching: Narsimha, Parshvanath, Buddha, Guru Ram Das Ji. (4 marks)

42. What do the words Param and atma mean? (2 marks)

43. Write the Indian names for Sunday and Monday. (2 marks)

44. Give three reasons why prayer is a principle of Dharma. (3 marks)

45. What is Dharma? (2 marks)

46. Why should we visit a friend's festival respectfully? (3 marks)

47. Name the three prayers studied in this lesson. (2 marks)

48. Give two ways water is used at home. (2 marks)

49. Explain the four Purusharthas with one example each for a child. (4 marks)

50. Explain why respect for the holy books of other faiths is important in Kenya. (5 marks)

51. Why is Saraswati shown with a veena and a book? (2 marks)

52. Describe how the boy in the example story practised Asteya. (3 marks)

53. Explain the meaning of Ahimsa and give two ways to practise it. (3 marks)

54. Why do the festival dates in this calendar change from year to year on our usual calendar? (2 marks)

55. Explain what the story of King Harishchandra teaches. (3 marks)

56. How can you learn more about the scriptures? Give four ways. (4 marks)

57. Match the days to the heavenly bodies: Ravivaar, Somvaar, Mangalvaar. (3 marks)

58. Describe how to do Bhastrika. (3 marks)

59. Explain why respect for a Mandir is important and how a visitor of any faith can show it. (5 marks)

60. Distinguish between Madaraka Day and Jamhuri Day. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — To compare seeds with water and seeds without water
   Comparing shows that water is needed for growth.

2. B — Collecting rainwater from a roof
   Roof water can be stored in a tank or jerrican.

3. C — Lake Victoria
   Lake Victoria is in Kenya; the other three are in India.

4. C — Vayu
   Wind is air, which is Vayu.

5. D — There are five
   Panch means five.

6. C — Hinduism
   Both are honoured especially in Hindu tradition.

7. C — At the doorway, neither inside nor outside
   Narsimha stopped him at the threshold.

8. C — Parshvanath
   Parshvanath is the twenty-third Tirthankar.

9. A — Varanasi
   Parshvanath was born as a prince in Varanasi.

10. A — Teachers
   Parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and holy teachers.

11. B — Equality
   Everyone sits side by side to eat.

12. D — The childhood of Ram and his brothers
   Bal means child.

13. C — Ram going to the forest and Bharat's humility
   It tells of Ram's fourteen years away from the kingdom.

14. D — A book of wise sayings and verses
   It teaches how to live wisely.

15. C — Listen to a teacher or recording for correct sounds
   Listening helps us say the right sounds.

16. C — Goddess of knowledge and learning
   Saraswati is the goddess of learning.

17. B — Slowly and clearly, sitting quietly
   Calm and clear.

18. B — A Hindu place of worship
   A Mandir is a Hindu temple.

19. B — Children, elders and people with disabilities
   We care for those who need help.

20. B — Harishchandra
   Harishchandra kept his word.

21. D — Good conduct
   Sadachaar is the way a good person behaves.

22. C — Honest even when nobody is watching
   Integrity is honesty at all times.

23. D — To keep found items until owners claim them
   Owners can claim their things.

24. B — Following the rules even when nobody is looking
   Fair play is integrity.

25. C — Keep it until you find a bin
   Keeping the environment clean is good conduct.

26. D — Sikhism
   Guru Nanak and Bhai Lalo.

27. C — To join or unite
   Yoga joins body, breath and mind.

28. D — A trained teacher or trusted adult
   An expert can prevent injury.

29. C — Paramatma
   Paramatma is God.

30. D — The right way of living
   Dharma includes duty, honesty and kindness.

31. C — They bring good results
   Good actions bring good results.

32. C — A living being
   Prani is a living creature.

33. C — King Shibi
   King Shibi saved the dove.

34. A — Be honest even when alone
   Honesty at all times.

35. D — Saving pocket money and not taking what is not yours
   Artha is honest wealth.

36. B — Micchami Dukkadam
   It asks for forgiveness.

37. B — Paryushan Parva
   It occurs in August or September.

38. A — Festival
   Utsav means festival.

39. C — That it is the night of Shiva and Parvati's wedding or of Shiva's great dance
   Different stories are told.

40. A — Day of the week
   Vaar means day.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha: God protects the good. Parshvanath: Ahimsa. Buddha: kindness to the hurt. Guru Ram Das Ji: honest work, equality and service.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct match.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Param means highest and atma means soul.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sunday: Ravivaar. Monday: Somvaar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes us thankful, calm and humble, gives courage, and reminds us we are not alone (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The right way of living, including duty, honesty and kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for two ideas.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: We listen, ask polite questions, do not laugh at customs, and build peace among communities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gayatri Mantra, Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva and Saraswati Vandana (any correct pair earns 1 mark).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark each, rounded up.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Drinking, cooking, washing, cleaning, watering plants or animals (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Dharma: doing homework and telling the truth. Artha: saving pocket money honestly. Kama: enjoying play and friendship. Moksha: praying and growing kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Kenya has people of many faiths, and respect helps us live in peace and unity. Making fun of another's holy book hurts feelings and causes conflict. Listening and learning builds understanding.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many faiths, 1 mark for peace and unity, 1 mark for hurt feelings, 1 mark for learning, 1 mark for a clear example.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: The veena stands for music and the arts and the book stands for knowledge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: He found a purse with money, did not keep it, and asked around until he found the owner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for three points.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ahimsa is not harming any living being by thought, word or action. We practise it by not bullying and by caring for animals and plants.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: The months follow the Moon, so the dates move.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: He gave up his kingdom rather than break his promise and never told a lie, so it teaches that truth is worth more than wealth and comfort.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the promise, 1 mark for truth, 1 mark for the lesson.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to a resource person, visit a temple or library, discuss with friends, watch a documentary, use a safe search engine with an adult (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sun, Moon, Mars.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit tall, breathe in deeply through the nose, breathe out through the nose with the same force, repeat slowly a few times, and rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sitting tall, 1 mark for equal in and out breaths, 1 mark for slow and rest.

59. (5 marks)
   Answer: A Mandir is a holy place. Visitors can remove shoes, dress modestly, speak softly, ask before photos and accept prasad politely. Respect brings peace among faiths.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for holy place, 3 marks for three ways, 1 mark for peace.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Madaraka Day is 1 June and marks internal self-government in 1963. Jamhuri Day is 12 December and marks independence in 1963 and the republic in 1964.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each date and 1 mark for a difference.
